Name: Polls
Summary: Ask visitors a question with a few options and show the results. Every visitor has one vote per poll.
Guide:
Polls appear on any page through a template function, for example on the home page or beside an article. Placing the instance on a page is optional; that page lists every poll.

Add it to the site

app.Use(polls.Module("polls", "Polls"))

The key (polls) is the instance's name in URLs and template functions and must be unique on the site. The title (Polls) is what editors see in the admin navigation and the page editor.

Write a poll

In the admin, open the instance (/admin/polls; /admin is the default admin path) and choose New poll:

  • Question, and an optional Short name, a name for templates such as favourite-colour.
  • Options: one per line, at least two and at most 20.
  • Closes at: when voting ends, in the site's timezone. Leave it empty to keep the poll open.
  • Show results before voting: otherwise visitors see the results after voting or once the poll is closed.

Publish the poll when it is ready. It appears in each language that has a question and at least two options.

Options are matched by line in every language, so translate them in the same order and add new options at the end. Changing the text of a line renames that option and keeps its votes. Options that have votes cannot be removed until the votes are reset.

New polls go to the top of the list, and editors can move them up and down. That order is the order of the polls function, and the top poll is the one {{pollBox "polls" ""}} shows. The list shows the number of votes per poll and which polls are closed.

Move to trash moves a poll to the trash with its votes, where it can be restored or deleted for good. Restoring is refused when another poll has taken its short name meanwhile.

Show a poll on any page

{{pollBox "polls" "favourite-colour"}}
{{pollBox "polls" ""}}

pollBox renders a published poll by short name or ID, or for "" the top poll of the list, the newest one unless editors moved the polls: the question, the vote form, the results with bars when they may be shown, and a notice after voting. Without such a poll it renders nothing.

The box comes with plain, accessible default markup. A theme replaces it with <key>/box.gohtml, or polls/box.gohtml for every instance; task templates -- polls writes the default to start from. It uses stable wt-* classes (wt-poll, wt-poll__results, wt-poll__bar, …), laid out by the optional stylesheet webthings.css, which the layout links with {{styles "webthings.css" "site.css"}} (see The base stylesheet). A result's bar is a <meter class="wt-poll__bar" min="0" max="100" aria-hidden="true"> whose value is the result's percentage, which also shows as text; it has no style attribute. webthings.css draws it as a --wt-bar track filled with --wt-accent. go-form renders the options with the site's form theme, as a fieldset with the question as its legend, by default wt-form__field wt-form__fieldset around wt-form__options with a wt-form__option each. Its texts go through tl, so the site's translations translate them.

For markup of your own, poll returns one poll (or nil), polls the first published polls ({{polls "polls" 0}} for all) and pollURL the address votes are posted to:

{{with poll "polls" "favourite-colour"}}
    <section id="{{.Anchor}}">
        <h2>{{.Question}}</h2>
        {{if eq .Result "voted"}}<p>Thanks for voting.</p>{{end}}

        {{if .CanVote}}
            {{form_open .Form}}
                {{form_field .Form "poll" nil}}
                {{form_field .Form "option" nil}}
                <button>Vote</button>
            {{form_close}}
        {{end}}

        {{if .ShowResults}}
            {{range .Options}}
                <p>{{.Label}}: {{.Percent}}%{{if .Chosen}} (your vote){{end}}</p>
                <meter min="0" max="100" value="{{.Percent}}">{{.Percent}}%</meter>
            {{end}}
            <p>{{.Total}} votes</p>
        {{end}}
    </section>
{{end}}

CanVote is set while the poll is open and the visitor has not voted. Percent is rounded, ClosesAt is in the site's timezone and zero for a poll that stays open.

.Form is the vote form: form_open writes the form tag, posting to .Action, with the spam trap and the page to return to, the element whose id is .Anchor (<key>-<poll ID>), so several polls can share a page. poll is a hidden field with the poll's ID. option renders the poll's options as radio buttons, required, in a fieldset with the question as its legend, in the site's form theme; the ids start with .Anchor. See Template functions. Radio inputs written by hand, named option with an option's .ID as value, work too.

Poll page

In the admin, open a page and choose the instance under Shows on this page. The page renders polls/list.gohtml with a polls.ListView: the page's published title, the instance key and every published poll in the editors' order. task templates -- polls writes a starting point for it too. The box works here:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/polls.ListView */}}
<h1>{{.Title}}</h1>

{{range .Polls}}
    {{pollBox $.Key .ID}}
{{end}}

Voting

The vote form posts to /_/<key>/vote ({{pollURL "polls"}}) with the fields of polls.VoteInput, poll (the poll's ID) and option (an option's ID), plus the spam trap and the way back that form_open adds. The visitor returns to the poll's .Anchor on the page with ?<key>=<result>&<key>_poll=<poll ID>. Only that poll gets the result as .Result, so other polls on the page show none; unknown results are ignored:

  • voted: the vote was counted;
  • already: this visitor already voted on this poll;
  • closed: the poll is closed or no longer published;
  • invalid: no option, or an option of another poll, was chosen;
  • throttled: more than 20 votes in a minute from this visitor; nothing was counted.

With invalid, the poll shows the vote form again with the message in the page's language at its options. The box and form_field do this without a change to the template; inputs written by hand do not. See A post with mistakes. A vote that fails for another reason, such as an unreachable database, gets the site's error page, 500.gohtml.

Bots that fill in the spam trap are told their vote counted; nothing is stored.

The first vote sets a wt_poll cookie that recognises the visitor for a year. Visitors without it are recognised by their IP address, so scripts that drop cookies get one vote per address; behind a reverse proxy, list it in Config.TrustedProxies. When someone else on that address already voted, the visitor gets a cookie of their own and can vote next time. Only a hash of the visitor's ID is stored, and addresses are keyed with a secret of the instance first, so votes cannot be traced back to addresses.

Only the cookie marks a poll as voted on a page. The module names it to the site's output cache (Env.PersonalCookie), which keeps pages apart for each value of wt_poll, so a visitor who voted sees their choice and others the vote form; see Modules and the output cache. Only a vote that counted makes the cache render the pages again: every other result tells it that nothing changed (frontend.NothingChanged).

Results

Results on the instance's admin page (/admin/polls/results) shows every poll with its status (draft, open or closed), the votes and percentage per option and the total. Reset votes removes all votes of a poll after confirmation; it needs the delete right.

From Go

polls.Of(app, "polls") returns the instance once the app has started. Latest and Find take the visitor's request, or nil, to mark what that visitor chose; Latest with a limit of 0 or less returns all polls:

survey := polls.Of(app, "polls")

newest, err := survey.Latest(ctx, nil, "en", 1)
poll, err := survey.Find(ctx, r, "en", "favourite-colour")

Vote counts a vote for any visitor ID, such as a member number, and returns ErrAlreadyVoted, ErrClosed or ErrInvalidOption; ResetVotes clears a poll. Store() gives write access for seed data. Votes and resets made from Go, and writes through Store(), show at once, also on pages in the site's output cache; see Modules and the output cache. Code may choose its own option IDs, unique in the poll and at most 36 bytes:

store := survey.Store()

saved, err := store.Save(ctx, content.Draft[polls.Fields, polls.Text]{
    Fields: polls.Fields{Options: polls.Lines{"red", "green", "blue"}},
    Translations: content.SetText(nil, "en", polls.Text{
        Question: "Which colour should the new logo have?",
        Slug:     "logo-colour",
        Options:  polls.Lines{"Red", "Green", "Blue"},
    }),
})

err = store.Publish(ctx, saved.ID, "", "en")

Related modules

  • Forms asks longer questions, with an inbox for the answers.
  • Comments lets visitors say more than a vote.

Funcs.Name: poll
Funcs.Doc: find returns one published poll for the current visitor, for example {{with poll "survey" "favourite-colour"}}, or nil.

Funcs.Name: pollBox
Funcs.Doc: pollBox renders the box component of one published poll, by slug or ID, or of the newest one when slugOrID is empty, for example {{pollBox "survey" "favourite-colour"}}. Without such a poll it renders nothing.

Funcs.Name: pollURL
Funcs.Doc: actionURL is the address vote forms post to, for example <form method="post" action="{{pollURL "survey"}}">, or "" for an unknown instance.

Funcs.Name: polls
Funcs.Doc: latest returns up to limit published polls, newest first unless editors reordered them, for example {{range polls "survey" 1}} on the home page; a limit of 0 or less returns all of them.

SQL.Name: postgres
SQL.SQL:
-- Polls are a collection (see package content). Option IDs are a JSON array
-- shared by all languages (UUIDs from the editor, or any IDs of at most 36
-- characters from code); each translation holds the option labels in the
-- same order.
CREATE TABLE wt_poll (
    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    instance     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    published    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    position     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_by   UUID,
    updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_by   UUID,
    deleted_at   TIMESTAMPTZ,
    deleted_by   UUID,
    option_ids   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    closes_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    show_results BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE
);

CREATE INDEX wt_poll_instance ON wt_poll (instance, position);

CREATE TABLE wt_poll_translation (
    item_id       UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES wt_poll (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    locale        VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    question      VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    slug          VARCHAR(190) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    option_labels TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, locale)
);

CREATE INDEX wt_poll_slug ON wt_poll_translation (locale, slug);

-- One vote per visitor and poll. visitor is the SHA-256 of the visitor's id
-- (see package polls), never the id or address itself.
CREATE TABLE wt_poll_vote (
    poll_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES wt_poll (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    instance   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    option_id  VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL,
    visitor    CHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (poll_id, visitor)
);

CREATE INDEX wt_poll_vote_instance ON wt_poll_vote (instance, visitor);

-- Polls are a collection (see package content). Option IDs are a JSON array
-- shared by all languages (UUIDs from the editor, or any IDs of at most 36
-- characters from code); each translation holds the option labels in the
-- same order.
CREATE TABLE wt_poll (
    id           VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
    instance     VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    published    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    position     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at   DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    created_by   VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    updated_at   DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    updated_by   VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    deleted_at   DATETIME(6) NULL,
    deleted_by   VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    option_ids   TEXT NOT NULL,
    closes_at    DATETIME(6) NULL,
    show_results BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    INDEX wt_poll_instance (instance, position)
) ENGINE=InnoDB;

CREATE TABLE wt_poll_translation (
    item_id       VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL,
    locale        VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    question      VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    slug          VARCHAR(190) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    option_labels TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (item_id, locale),
    INDEX wt_poll_slug (locale, slug),
    FOREIGN KEY (item_id) REFERENCES wt_poll (id) ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB;

-- One vote per visitor and poll. visitor is the SHA-256 of the visitor's id
-- (see package polls), never the id or address itself.
CREATE TABLE wt_poll_vote (
    poll_id    VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL,
    instance   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    option_id  VARCHAR(36) NOT NULL,
    visitor    CHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    created_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (poll_id, visitor),
    INDEX wt_poll_vote_instance (instance, visitor),
    FOREIGN KEY (poll_id) REFERENCES wt_poll (id) ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB;

Types.Name: Fields
Types.Doc: Fields are the language-independent parts of a poll. Options are the option IDs in their order; votes refer to them. The editor makes UUIDs; code that writes polls through Store may use any IDs that are unique in the poll, not empty and at most 36 bytes, and must keep them once there are votes.

Types.Name: Item
Types.Doc: Item is a stored poll with its translations.

Types.Name: Lines
Types.Doc: Lines is a list of strings stored as a JSON array in one column.

Types.Name: ListView
Poll
Types.Doc: Poll is a poll as templates see it, with the results and what the current visitor did.

Types.Name: ResultRow
Types.Doc: ResultRow is one poll with its options and their votes.

Types.Name: ResultsView
Types.Doc: ResultsView is the data of templates/admin/results.gohtml: the votes of every poll.

Types.Name: Service
Types.Doc: Service is one Polls instance, for the website's own code.

Types.Name: Text
Types.Doc: Text is a poll in one language. Options are the labels of Fields.Options, in the same order.

Types.Name: VoteInput
Types.Doc: VoteInput is the vote a visitor posts to /_/<key>/vote: the poll's ID and the chosen option's ID. Poll.Form is its model for a poll, with the poll's options (RenderModel.Options) and its question as the label of the options: form_open, {{form_field .Form "poll" nil}} and {{form_field .Form "option" nil}} render the form, the options as radio buttons. A poll that does not exist answers "closed"; a vote without an option, or with one the poll does not have, answers "invalid", and the poll shows the vote again with the message at its options (frontend.KeepForm).
